name: keeparr
description: Keeparr helps everyone on your media server decide what's worth KEEPING — and reports what can safely be deleted to reclaim space. HOW IT WORKS • Everyone on your Plex (or Jellyfin/Emby) server signs in and gets a "For You"-style Keep feed — a screenful of titles at a time, weighted toward the biggest space-hogs, so decisions happen a few at a time instead of all at once. • For each title: Keep, "I don't care", or — for titles they requested via Seerr — "OK to delete" (the requester signing off). • Keeps are protective: if anyone keeps a title, it's safe. • The Big Picture dashboard shows what's reclaimable, what nobody has watched, and per-quality storage breakdowns. NOTHING GETS DELETED Unlike rule-based cleanup tools (e.g. Maintainerr), Keeparr never deletes anything — it crowdsources the human decisions and hands you the report; you delete in your media server or Sonarr/Radarr. INTEGRATIONS (ALL OPTIONAL) Tautulli watch history, Overseerr/Jellyseerr requests, and any number of Sonarr/Radarr instances for quality/tag data and match health. SETUP No required config beyond the port and appdata path — secrets are auto-generated on first start. The first user to sign in becomes the admin, so complete first-run setup on your trusted LAN before exposing Keeparr to the internet.

paths.name: Appdata
paths.description: Keeparr's database, poster cache and backups.

paths.name: Media (optional, read-only)
paths.description: Optional. Mount a media share read-only so Keeparr can show array capacity / free space (map libraries to paths in Settings → Connections). Add more paths for more shares.

ports.name: WebUI Port
ports.description: Host port for the Keeparr web UI.

variables.name: SESSION_SECRET
variables.description: Optional — leave EMPTY and Keeparr auto-generates a secret on first start (stored in appdata as .session-secret). Set it only to manage the secret yourself; if you do, use a HIGH-ENTROPY value (e.g. `openssl rand -hex 32`) — it signs sessions AND encrypts your stored Plex/Tautulli/Seerr/Sonarr/Radarr tokens, so a weak value is unsafe. Never change it once in use.

variables.name: APP_URL
variables.description: Optional. Public URL of this app (e.g. https://keeparr.example.net) — used for the Plex sign-in redirect when behind a reverse proxy.

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: User ID the app runs as. Keeparr fixes ownership of the appdata path to this on start. Unraid default is 99 (nobody).

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: Group ID the app runs as. Unraid default is 100 (users).
